visualReview.notes: Compared the court elevation to the dated photograph. The reconstruction includes the lower round brick arcade, a deep upper veranda with square piers and turned balusters, a long tiled hip roof, and two stacks.

sharedSurfaceReview.notes: Inspected the shared brick, sandstone, lime plaster, clay tile, wood and dark fenestration. The dated geographic placement and its bounded ground opening loaded and unloaded cleanly.

mediumFiReview.notes: The roof, two floors and long seven-bay arcade remain distinct across all four authored levels. The closest model adds turned balusters, rounded veranda door heads, window divisions and eave detail.

terrain.grade: The original 280 m Copernicus GLO-30 surface spans 0 to 25.9009 m EGM2008. The court datum samples 13.7566 m. Modern structures in this surface obscure the lower arches on the west with the placement mask disabled. A bounded mask just inside the modeled stone terrace preserves the historic arcade floor in the dated placement. The surrounding modern surface is retained and can still obscure the terrace from low, distant cameras.

geographicReview.notes: The historic premises are tied to the Medical Missionary Hospital on the 1880 Canton map and to the current independently mapped hospital area in Guangzhou. The exact footprint and alignment of this individual west-campus wing are estimated.

fidelityReview.scope: The late nineteenth-century verandah-fronted building photographed at Dr. Kerr’s Canton Hospital on the Renji Road premises in Guangzhou.
fidelityReview.notes: Represents the nineteenth-century hospital block in the photograph, in the period discussed in the Qualla story. Dimensions, end bays obscured by foliage, side and rear window schedules, material colors, historic grade and exact position inside the known site are approximate.

imageryReview.notes: The Qualla illustration concerns a later design. Viewed the original November 7, 1895 New York issue of The Evangelist from the Internet Archive. Its dated cover includes the photograph and credits E. Warren Clark.

validation.sharedCaptureScope: Inspected 43 final frames, including the court elevation, brick and veranda details, reconstructed rear wall, shared materials, geographic placement, and all four detail levels, plus the unmasked original terrain.

limitations: The model depicts the single wing shown in the 1895 photograph. It covers an earlier phase than the twentieth-century campus and later design published with the story.

The photographed front scale uses people, arch spacing and floor height. Behind-tree bays, the back, width and pitch of the roof, window schedules, material colors and block position are approximations. The independent mapped boundary represents the successor campus.
Modern urban structures influence the source DSM. The archival evidence does not establish the courtyard’s historic height.
